scope: Text-only native adapters; five additional checkpoints, four families; one independent worker per checkpoint in this pilot. Not confirmatory or production certification.

admission.states: Eight calibration templates; typed questions and 2/4/8/16 choice candidates
admission.scope_of_evidence: Finite tested inputs and sizes; no per-future-request fidelity guarantee

traces: homogeneous ordered choice schema with diverse lengths
diverse decision kinds, candidate widths, lengths and reordered schemas
baselines: released native batching at size <=8, grouped by schema with FIFO order

accounting: all exposed native decision fields and per-request usage
serving.limitation: 6-11 second arrival windows, not the future three independent 30-minute trials

profiling: Tensor model native operator profiles; JEV worker CUDA trace separately collected after shared timing with profiler disabled throughout measurement.
infrastructure: CPU preparation completed before GPU allocation. One study GPU across apps; production apps untouched. Failed attempts and export failures retained.
hypothesis: Released native batching plus contract-aware selection can handle changed traffic without custom per-shape recapture. Improvement over serial alone is batching evidence, not a novel DFIP gain; compare against native batching.
falsification: Retain admission failures, native variation, output changes, fallbacks, drops and slowdowns. If shared policy cannot outperform native batching with acceptable finite-test fidelity, general acceleration remains unproven.
